summary: Ch.1: Chris Comerford (20, omega) recovers memories of a past life as a pharmacist and realises he is a doomed side character in a BL novel: married to King Allen for an heir, then killed with his son. To survive he plans to stay childless, posing as a 'defective omega' with inhibitors he brews himself. Allen coldly says Chris is only there to bear his child and to send word at his heat. Two months pass with no heat; Allen comes to question him, senses Chris has changed, and leaves when Chris politely asks him to tend to his duties.

Ch.2: Chris meets Allen in the palace library corridor, notices he is feverish and treats him at the White Rose Palace; Allen struggles to say thank you. Allen starts visiting often, then asks Chris for an aphrodisiac and asks if he is jealous; Chris says he cannot object. Allen drinks it himself and forces himself on Chris, who did not want it (scene left untranslated). Afterwards Allen apologises, confesses he likes Chris since Chris began keeping his distance, and promises to treasure him; Chris is stunned.

Ch.3: Allen now visits Chris every night; Chris, without an excuse to refuse, is worn out and wonders if saying he still loved Allen was a mistake. On his heat day (hidden with suppressants) Chris invites Allen to tea and spikes it with a slow sedative; Allen mentions an upcoming diplomatic trip to Orvent. The maid takes the drowsy Allen to Chris's own bed. Allen has a nightmare, calls 'Dad, don't leave me', asks Chris to hold his hand while they sleep; Chris finds it not so bad. First night together without sex.

Ch.4: Allen leaves on a month-long mission to Orvent and kisses Chris goodbye in public. In the library Chris meets Nathaniel, Allen's official spouse, who later sends a hand mirror (a veiled insult) and invites him to tea, where his palace ladies mock Chris's looks. Chris retorts with a rotten-apple remark. Chris catches himself missing Allen. Allen returns with rare herb seeds and asks for a kiss as a reward, then carries Chris off to the bedroom. Nathaniel vows not to let the consort beat him.

Ch.5: Allen fends off Nathaniel's night invitations to stay with Chris; Nathaniel seethes. He drags Chris to the Red Rose Palace greenhouse and demands he either have his womb destroyed or give up being consort, then slaps him; Chris calls his bluff and offers him a sleeping potion for his dark circles. Allen arrives having heard the maids; Chris covers for Nathaniel, claiming they fought equally. Days later Nathaniel accepts the tonic, reveals he too is rumoured a defective omega (heats but no child), and asks whether Chris truly is one.

Ch.6: Autumn; Allen still dotes on Chris. He takes Chris to a dinner at the Mulligan estate (Nathaniel declined, unwell). Chris expects Colin Mulligan, newly revealed omega, to be offered as another concubine, which would free him; instead the Mulligans announce Colin will take a son-in-law. Colin greets Chris warmly. On the way back Allen turns cold; Chris tells himself that is what he wanted, yet it hurts.

Ch.7: Jealous after Chris smiled at Colin, Allen takes him roughly as a "punishment" (scene left untranslated). In the morning he apologises; Chris reassures him his heart belongs to him, while privately keeping up the act. Allen proposes a honeymoon: they stay in a Mulligan cabin to see the autumn leaves. Allen says the cabin is haunted and suggests a test of courage that night; Chris, preferring a ghost to sex, agrees, but Allen still wants time together first.

Haunted-cottage test of courage: the 'ghost' is a mirror Allen planted ten years ago as a prank on Colin and the others. Allen sees Colin and his siblings as little brothers, wishes Colin happiness and promises to make Chris happy too; Chris wonders what happiness is to him. Allen catches a cold; Chris picks herbs and brews an infusion; they promise to return next autumn. Chris knows that by then, in the original story, Nathaniel carries Allen's child, and feels conflicted. Back at the Red Rose Palace he hands out tea from the Mulligan domain; the palace staff remind him to knit a blue scarf for Allen's winter birthday (eye-coloured scarf tradition); Nathaniel will give one too, which leaves Chris uneasy.

Ch.9: Chris gives Allen the blue shawl the night before the birthday banquet; Allen, delighted, spends the night with him. At the banquet Allen enters with Nathaniel wearing Nathaniel's shawl, and Chris, hurt, tells himself it is natural and he should go back to being the neglected consort. Colin notices he is forcing a smile. On the balcony Allen finds Chris: he wore Chris's shawl all along except for the entrance, and wraps it around the cold Chris; Chris gives it back and sends him in to greet the guests with Nathaniel. Chris finally admits to himself that he loves Allen.

Ch.10: After the banquet Allen leads Chris to the empty chapel and holds a private wedding for the two of them (concubines get no wedding in Zilfonia), swearing to love him forever. He then insists on consummating it there; Chris gives in, even gets on top for his birthday, and realises he is head over heels. Chris confesses "I love you" and Allen answers in kind, then wants to continue at the palace.

Ch.11: Spring. Allen arranges for Chris to visit the Comerford estate for three days for his birthday (consorts normally may never leave the palace), on condition he comes too. On the way Allen, an only child who treats Colin as a little brother, lists the ideal partner for Colin. Chris's father, papa and younger brother Ted welcome them; Allen and Chris get separate rooms. Ted, cold to Allen, asks what he likes about his brother and is scolded; Allen says he loves everything about Chris, stunning Ted. Alone at night Chris finds he misses Allen and pleasures himself thinking of him.

Ch.12: Missing Allen, Chris goes to his room and asks him to make love; afterwards he is embarrassed it was his own doing. The Marquis privately urges Chris to love Allen with all he has, hinting Allen's papa did not simply leave him; Chris suspects his papa died, perhaps by choice, and that Allen's doting is fear of being abandoned. Chris promises always to stay by Allen's side. On the way back Allen reveals the First and Second Princes of Orvent are visiting and asks Chris and Nathaniel to host the Second Prince; Chris worries about slighting Nathaniel, eldest son of the powerful Marquis Abernathy.

Ch.13: Waiting with Nathaniel for the Orvent princes, Chris learns the Second Prince Noah is an omega rumoured to become Allen's second consort. Noah proves cheerful and innocent, delighting in Nathaniel's rose garden and Chris's herb garden. At the welcoming ball Chris meets the First Prince Julian; Nathaniel explains minister Calvin proposed Noah as consort and wants Chris as an ally, since he could beat Chris but not Noah. Allen dances with Noah and Chris feels a pang of jealousy. Julian invites Chris to dance; Chris trips, Julian catches him and insists on carrying him to a doctor.

Ch.14: Allen takes the twisted-ankled Chris from Julian's arms; Chris, insecure, avoids Allen and feigns illness while Nathaniel hosts Noah. After the princes leave, Allen visits the Red Rose Palace, gives Chris a wedding band, admits jealousy over Julian, and reveals he refused minister Calvin's proposal to marry Noah -- Calvin seems in league with Julian to make Zilfonia Orvent's vassal. He will take no other consort because he loves Chris; they make love. Afterwards Chris realises the story has left the novel's plot and wonders who will bear Allen's heir.

Ch.15: The morning after, a servant reports that minister Calvin plans to seize the throne. Calvin arrives with soldiers and reveals Allen is really Nate Mulligan -- the late king's heir was stillborn and a Mulligan newborn was swapped in on the king's order -- so Allen must be deposed and tried for posing as royalty. The Red Rose Palace knights, joined by Marquis Comerford's private army and Nathaniel, cover their escape. In the carriage the Marquis confirms the story; after two weeks they reach an old run-down Comerford manor. The Marquis says Calvin will crown a beta descendant of the former King Jack with Noah as official husband, that the Comerford and likely Mulligan houses back Allen, and urges him to retake the throne; Allen asks for time to think.

Ch.16: Nathaniel urges Chris to go to Allen, who confesses his omega father rejected him as an impostor, was thought mad and took his own life. Allen muses about abandoning the throne to live quietly with Chris, who longs for it but reminds him of Calvin's danger and his people. The Marquis brings news that Calvin, as an orphanage director, sold the most beautiful and talented children to Orvent as slaves. Allen resolves to retake the throne, thanks his loyal allies, and asks the Marquis to rally the nobles who support him.

Ch.17: Over two months allied nobles gather at the manor while Calvin is backed only by Marquis Abernathy -- and by Orvent, whose army enters the royal castle. Nathaniel, whose family sides with Calvin, stays and expects Chris to become official husband once Allen wins. The Marquis plans to expose Calvin's orphan trafficking to turn the people. The night before the march Allen thanks Chris for giving him the resolve and promises to return; Chris says he will tell him something when he does. In Orvent's capital Calvin reports to Julian, who privately despises him. Allen leaves with the army as Chris fears he will be beheaded if they lose.

Ch.18: On the march Allen reflects that his early clinging to Chris came from his omega father's abandonment, but now he truly loves Chris, who taught him to love and be loved. His birth father Marquis Mulligan joins him; Allen thanks him for his life and asks to call him father after the war. The citizens of the capital oppose Calvin. Near the capital Orvent's royal knights block the way, but Prince Noah arrives, turns against his brother Julian's plot and holds them off so Allen can press on. At the manor Chris frets; Colin, worried for his own fiancé, cheers him up, and Nathaniel tells him to stay strong as Allen's main spouse until the outcome is decided.

Ch.19: Through summer into autumn Chris waits until Allen's side wins and he returns as promised. In the dungeon Calvin rages that Allen has no royal blood; Allen answers that he will tell his people the truth and leave with his husband if they reject him. In the capital he reveals he is Nate Mulligan without royal blood and asks to keep protecting the kingdom; the people acclaim him. Calvin and the pretender stay imprisoned and his noble supporters lose their lands. Back at the manor Chris confesses he faked being a defective omega; Allen, unbothered, asks him to be his official husband as the new king Nate Mulligan, since Nathaniel's family sided with Calvin and, above all, he wants Chris. Chris says he loves him and wishes to bear his child; they promise to stay together forever.
